 Amazon Shares Drop as Huge AI Spending and Ad Revenue Miss Weigh on Q3 Results
Amazon shares slumped as much as 13% in extended trading after the company reported a third-quarter revenue miss and a projection for fourth-quarter profit that trailed analyst estimates. The company's advertising division brought in $19.6B, missing the $20.87B expected, while total net sales reached $201.9B against a $202.3B estimate. The decline was driven by a surge in capital expenditures for artificial intelligence infrastructure, which totaled $77.3B for the quarter—nearly $20B above forecasts—resulting in a trailing twelve-month free cash flow of negative $42.4B.
The losses in market value followed a report otherwise marked by efficiency and cloud strength, including a record operating margin of 13.9% and Amazon Web Services revenue growth of 39% to $46B. AWS currently operates at an annualized run rate of $184B, with Chief Executive Officer Andy Jassy forecasting growth rates above 40% for both 2027 and 2028. To sustain this expansion, the company maintained its cash capital expenditure forecast of approximately $220B for 2026, while Jassy suggested that the company's long-term trajectory could lead to multiple businesses generating $1 trillion in annual revenue within the next decade.
